body:
**Starts** once #53 is merged.

## Why

Each waypoint carries a reason, in the coordinator's own words, such as "steer onto US-1", "must-see: Capitol Reef", or "the user asked: the Golden Gate Bridge" (domain model 3.6). #166 added it. The reason shows in every itinerary read, and in the replies of `set_waypoints` and `update_day` (tool design 2.1). It has two readers:

- **The coordinator.** When the user approves fastest on a day, code clears all of the day's waypoints, and `update_day`'s reply lists each one with its reason. The coordinator puts back the ones for a must-see or the user's request, and drops the ones that only kept the drive on a scenic road (technical spec 5.2). In a later session, the reason is the only record of why a waypoint is there.
- **A person reading the itinerary,** who can spot a bad pick without opening a trace. Example: the Pulgas Water Temple waypoint (#163) would have read "steer onto I-280", though the temple sits off I-280.

The reason was added on reasoning, not measured. It costs context in every read, a few words per waypoint, on every turn. Nobody knows yet whether the coordinator uses it well, or whether it would do as well without it. An evaluation should show whether the reasons earn their place, and if not, what to change.

There's also a design choice to weigh. The design names exactly three kinds of reason: a scenic road, a must-see, and the user's request. A set fixed by the design could be an enum on the waypoint, beside the free text. Then code could clear only the scenic waypoints when fastest is approved, and the coordinator's put-back step would go away. Today code clears them all "because a reason is the coordinator's own words, which code can't sort" (technical spec 5.2).

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), 4.2 (how a waypoint is picked) and 5.2 (approving fastest).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), 3.6 (Day: waypoints), 4.5 (`DaysService.approveRouteType()`), and 4.7 (how a leg is routed).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), 2.1: `set_waypoints`, `update_day`, and `read_itinerary`.
- #163 and #166, for how reasons came about, with the traces that showed the problem.
- #53, for how evaluations are set up and run.

## Open questions

- What does the evaluation measure? Proposal: whether, after the user approves fastest on a day in a new session, the coordinator puts back exactly the must-see and user-asked waypoints, and drops the scenic ones. Code scores it from what was saved. A second question, whether having to write a reason leads to better picks (a place on the road, not a sight beside it), needs a judge or a road-time rule, so it waits until the first results show whether reasons matter.
- What's the comparison? Proposal: run the case as the design stands, then with the reasons left out of `update_day`'s reply and the reads. If the coordinator keeps the right waypoints just as well without them, the reasons serve only people, and could be stored but not shown to the model.
- Is the reason-kind enum tried here? Proposal: decide after the first results. If the coordinator often keeps or drops the wrong waypoints, the enum lets code do it instead.
- How many runs? Proposal: 5 for each variant.

## Do

- Write the evaluation, with a trip whose day has one scenic waypoint, one for a must-see, and one the user asked for. Run it as the design stands, and with the reasons hidden. Record the results in this issue.
- Look at the results and traces with Joe, and decide: keep the reasons as they are, keep them but hide them from the model, or add the enum. If the design changes, the implementer drafts the change, and Joe reviews it in the PR.

## Done when

- The results are recorded for each variant.
- The evaluation stays in the set, so later changes rerun it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A decision, or a PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.
